segments.text:
V. 27.
He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living—That is, (if the Argument be propſed at length) Since the Character of his being the GOD of any Perſons, plainly intimates a Relation to them, not as dead, but as living; and ſince He cannot be ſaid to be at preſent their GOD at all, if they are utterly dead; nor to be the GOD of human Perſons, ſuch as Abraham, Iſaac, and Iacob, conſiſting of Souls and Bodies, if their Bodies were to abide in everlaſting Death: there muſt needs be a ſuture State of Bleſſedneſs, and a Reſurrection of the Body to ſhare with the Soul in it.
